newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria plans new oil exploration tender for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria plans new oil exploration tender for 1997.

text.p: Bulgaria will call its third oil exploration tender in 1997, an official said on Thursday.
"The tender will be for more than 10 blocks onshore following the advice of a foreign firm," Simeon Kalaidjiev, chairman of Bulgaria's Geology and Mineral Resources Committee told Reuters.
He denied newspaper reports that Texaco Inc and Britain's Enterprise Oil Plc, licensed to explore for oil and gas, were cancelling their contracts and leaving Bulgaria.
Kalaidjiev said Texaco had completed its second drilling, aimed at evaluating the gas volumes in a well they found in their Black Sea block southeast of the port of Varna in 1993.
"We are waiting for the results of the tests and I am optimistic that the gas they found will be of commercial importance," he said.
Texaco works together with Enterprise and Austria's OMV AG. Officials said the investment of the three companies was expected to total $40 million by the year-end.
Kalaidjiev said Enterprise had also completed its drillings in Block Two on the Black Sea shelf near Cape Kaliakra in northeastern Bulgaria.
"Next year they are planning to drill in their block at the Ropotamo river," he said.
